newsitem.title: USA: Ashland Q1 hurt by several items.
newsitem.headline: Ashland Q1 hurt by several items.

text.p: Ashland Inc Tuesday reported a slight decline in first quarter profits, excluding the non-recurring gain a year ago, saying it was due primarily to lower results from refining and marketing, Ashland Coal and its construction subsidiary.

New income in the quarter ended December 31 was $36 million, or $0.47 a share, down from $87 million, or $1.29 a share, a year earlier, which included an after-tax gain of $48 million, or $0.74 cents per share, from the settlement of Ashland Exploration's claims in the Columbia Gas bankruptcy reorganization.

In keeping with industry practice, Ashland said, it began allocating more of the costs of doing business to operating divisions effective October 1, 1996. This reduced segment operating income by a total of $11 million but had no impact on overall operating or net income. Prior-year results will not be restated.
Ashland Chemical was the leading contributor to the quarter, with $34 million in operating income.
"Ashland Chemical had a good, solid quarter," Chief Executive Officer Paul W. Chellgren said.
"Results from specialty chemical businesses continued to grow, while operating income from distribution remained strong. The combination somewhat offset lower petrochemical profits."
With $18 million in operating profit, Ashland said, its APAC highway construction group was the second largest contributor to earnings, although results declined somewhat from the quarter last year.
"Adverse weather conditions in several of APAC's operating areas reduced construction activity and led to lower volumes," Chellgren said.
"The backlog, however, remains strong at $564 million and contains favorable margins."

Valvoline had excellent results, with operating income of $13 million. The U.S. lubricant business was the leading contributor to earnings, reflecting strong motor oil margins. Operating income from automotive chemical, coolant and antifreeze businesses all improved. Stronger results from Valvoline International and the First Recovery used oil collection also contributed to higher operating income.

Excluding the unusual gain in the quarter a year ago, Ashland Exploration's operating income doubled to $12 million. An $0.89 per thousand cubic feet increase in the average gas price was the largest contributor to the improvement.

Ashland said it is now reporting the results of Ashland Petroleum, its refining division, and SuperAmerica retail gasoline marketing operations as a single industry segment. Combined results from these operations totaled $14 million.
"Rapidly rising crude oil prices late in the quarter led to an operating loss in December and were a key factor in disappointing results for the quarter," Chellgren commented.

Increased sales volumes and lower costs led to a good quarter for Arch Mineral. Equity income of $5 million was nearly three times higher than last year's December quarter. Ashland Coal had a reasonably good quarter despite the continuing adverse effects of several contract expirations at the end of calendar 1995. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
